data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is less resilient than a large service if the independence of operators is merely a perceived surface condition masking a shared latent cause (e.g., a common cloud provider or open-source dependency), because the correlated failure mode dominates once the shared cause triggers.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services have formally disjoint software and infrastructure stacks (e.g., formally verified independence).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service itself shares a hidden critical dependency with a smaller backup system, making the redundancy a mere appearance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Common-cause failures propagate through shared hidden dependencies; the monolith's strictly greater internal redundancy eliminates the same single point of failure, whereas decentralized services independently build the same hidden vulnerability (e.g., all using the same DNS provider).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
